resources.string: This window shows Whittle as it runs on your phone: your chats, files and settings. They stay on the phone; nothing is copied here.
Only computers you add on the phone can open the tunnel, and only with its token.
Turn on Use from your computer
On your phone: Settings › Linux workspace. Its address is on the Wi-Fi chip there.
In a terminal on this computer; leave it running.
Read it from the phone with this, then paste it here.
The phone didn't accept that token.
Copy it again with the command in step 3; it changes when Linux is reset.
Check that Use from your computer is on and the tunnel in step 2 is still running.
The tunnel may have closed, or the phone went to sleep. Open the tunnel again and connect.
Opens http://127.0.0.1:%1$d in this computer's browser. The server runs on your phone, so its port needs a tunnel too: ssh -L %1$d:127.0.0.1:%1$d phone
It isn't serving yet; try again once its card says it's live.
Connections, phone features, the assistant and updates are in Whittle on your phone.
